sections.h2: What makes Carroll County, Kentucky, different for a house seller?
sections.html:
Carroll County is a small river county where the Kentucky River meets the Ohio, and its seat, Carrollton, sits at that confluence. At 128.68 square miles of land it is the third-smallest county in Kentucky by area, and the 2020 Census counted 10,810 residents. Carrollton lies about 54 miles from Cincinnati and 55 from Louisville along U.S. 42, with Interstate 71 about four miles south of town.

That location shapes who buys here. The county's own website lists employers such as North American Stainless, CertainTeed and Kentucky Utilities, and describes General Butler State Resort Park, a 791-acre park, as a local draw. Jefferson Community College serves the county. A house in Carrollton is often sold to a worker commuting along the river or I-71 corridor, and Carrollton itself was laid out in 1792 under the name Port William.

The city itself is compact, about two square miles with 3,890 residents in 2020. Prestonville lies across the Kentucky River to the west, and Switzerland County, Indiana, sits across the Ohio to the north. The county's own site adds that the Kentucky Veterans Memorial is in Carrollton and that boats launch from Point Park.

Carrollton's worst recorded flood was the Ohio River flood of 1937, with a crest of 79.9 feet, according to Wikipedia. Sellers of low-lying homes near the river should ask the city planning office for floodplain information.

sections.h2: Which Carroll County office does what with a tax bill?
sections.html:
A parcel is valued by the PVA, billed by the Sheriff's Office, and handed to the County Clerk if it goes delinquent. The county's clerk page lists those delinquent collections beside recording deeds and mortgages and filing wills and probate orders.

  • Sheriff: first floor of the courthouse at 440 Main Street, (502) 732-7010, with online tax lookup and payment through the sheriff's page.
  • County Clerk: same building, (502) 732-7005, for delinquent taxes and deeds.
  • County administration: (502) 732-5448, the office that edits or exonerates county tax amounts when a bill looks wrong.

Carroll's FAQ puts the annual due date at December 31 and expects bills in October or November. An owner who has seen nothing should look the bill up on the sheriff's page. In the state's description, most counties begin collecting on October 1 or November 1. The exact discount cutoff is printed on the bill, and the sheriff's office can confirm it.

sections.h2: Can Carroll County owners split payments or get a late fee waived?
sections.html:
Neither. The county FAQ rules out a payment plan and requires the whole bill in one transaction. It also says that a bill that never arrived is not a permitted ground for waiving late fees under the state's administrative regulations.

Mixing tender is fine, such as part check and part cash or card. The penalty ladder comes from KRS 134.015:

  • On or before the discount date: 2% off.
  • Until December 31: the printed amount.
  • During January: 5% on the unpaid tax.
  • Past January 31: 10%.

The debt also becomes a lien. A Carrollton house with a past-due bill will be flagged by the buyer's title company, so line up the clerk's payoff figure early.

sections.h2: How does a Carroll County tax sale work?
sections.html:
After April 15 the sheriff hands unpaid bills to the County Clerk, and a sale comes at least 90 days afterward. KRS 134.128, summarized on the state's collection page, puts the sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer, with notices to the owner at 30 and 60 days.

The clerk sold Carroll's 2025 delinquent taxes on July 24, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. on the courthouse's second floor, with third-party purchasers registering by July 14, 2026. Questions go to the clerk at (502) 732-7005. A buyer who purchases a certificate may add substantial fees, which is why owners fare better paying before the sale.

In the state's first example, a $1,000 bill paid within five business days of reaching the clerk costs about $1,388 once interest, a clerk commission and a recording fee are added. Waiting brings in the county attorney's commission, postage and advertising costs.

sections.h2: How can a Carrollton owner appeal a value?
sections.html:
Ask the PVA for a conference, then file with the clerk once the roll closes. The roll stays open 13 days after the first Monday in May, and an appeal is valid only after a conference with the PVA or a deputy, as the state calendar sets out.

The PVA must send notice whenever it assesses above the value you listed. A deed price can also serve as the listed value for the next January 1 if the property has not changed. For a Carroll County seller who bought recently, that means the purchase price may be the PVA's starting point, so keep your closing statement.

The local board owes a written explanation for any increase or decrease, and you may record the hearing. Do not skip it, since not filing or not appearing ends your right to further review.

sections.h2: Which exemptions are open to Carroll County homeowners?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is available on a primary residence to owners aged 65 or more and to owners who are totally disabled. One state form, 62A350, covers both, and the PVA keeps it on file.

It deducts a set dollar amount from the assessed value, not the entire value, and the amount is reset every two years. A buyer cannot inherit it. Veterans with a total service-connected disability file once, as do owners found disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement System.

Ask the PVA for the current dollar amount, because the dollar figure published on the state's page covers a past assessment period. A seller who is 65 should confirm the exemption was applied before closing.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Carroll County homes?
sections.html:
A typical owner-occupied house in Carroll County is valued at $140,900 for 2020 to 2024, between Caldwell's $118,500 and Calloway's $183,200. Owners live in 65.7 percent of homes, the second-lowest share of the four counties, and the 2025 estimate of 11,141 residents is 3.1 percent above 2020.

The Census counted a single building permit in Carroll County in 2025, so most buyers are choosing among existing homes. Employers in Carroll County reported 6,600 jobs in 2023, with total payroll near $497 million, and employment rose 4.7 percent from 2022. Only 11.4 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and 17.3 percent of residents live in poverty, figures that sit beside the county's $140,900 median home value. Sellers who cannot wait for financing, or who are managing an estate or a rental with tenants, can sell as-is for cash and pay the tax payoff from the proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the Carroll County tax deadline?
faqs.a: December 31 is the annual due date, with a discount for bills paid by the early cutoff printed on your bill. January adds 5% and anything later adds 10%.

faqs.q: Does Carroll County allow a payment plan?
faqs.a: No. The county requires the full amount in a single transaction, though check, cash and card can be combined.

faqs.q: Whom do I call about delinquent Carroll County taxes?
faqs.a: The County Clerk, at (502) 732-7005, collects delinquent real estate taxes and runs the sale.

faqs.q: Is a late fee waived if my bill never came?
faqs.a: No. The county FAQ lists a missing bill as an impermissible reason for a waiver. Look the bill up on the sheriff's page each fall.

faqs.q: Can a Carrollton house with back taxes be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer can take it as-is and the payoff is paid from your proceeds at closing. Get the figure from the County Clerk before you sign.
